Source slide page 1 (extracted text):
PYTHON FOR COMPUTATIONAL
PROBLEM SOLVING
Introduction to the Course Title

 Prof. Sindhu R Pai
PCPS Theory Anchor - 2024
Department of Computer Science and Engineering

Source slide page 2 (extracted text):
PYTHON FOR COMPUTATIONAL PROBLEM SOLVING
 Course Overview

Course Objectives
  •  Learn syntax and semantics of Python programming language
  •  Illustrate the process of structuring data using lists, tuples, sets and dictionaries
  • Demonstrate use of built in functions to navigate the file system
  •  Learn various paradigms  of programming and implement Object-Oriented
    Programming concepts in Python
Course Outcomes
  At the end of this course, students will be able to:
  •  Program effectively using the Python language
  •  Identify the methods to create and manipulate lists, tuples, sets and dictionaries
  •  Discover commonly used operations using file system
  •  Think using different paradigms of programming and interpret the concepts of
    Object-Oriented Programming as used in Python
                                                                                                                                                                   2

Source slide page 5 (extracted text):
PYTHON FOR COMPUTATIONAL PROBLEM SOLVING
  Introduction

What does a computer do?
   Fundamentally performs calculations, remembers results


What types of calculations can a computer do?

    •  Basic built-in operations like simple arithmetic and logic

    • More complex operations derived from the built-in
     operations





                                                                                                                                                                      5

Source slide page 6 (extracted text):
PYTHON FOR COMPUTATIONAL PROBLEM SOLVING
  Introduction

Can a computer perform / solve any task at all?

  No, of course not!

   This gives us a basic classification of the types of tasks:

   •  Computational: Those which can be solved by computers
     Eg: Sorting a list of numbers, weather forecasting etc.

   •  Non-computational: Those which cannot be solved by computers
     Eg: Painting a picture, solving a moral dilemma etc.





                                                                                                                                                                      6

Source slide page 7 (extracted text):
PYTHON FOR COMPUTATIONAL PROBLEM SOLVING
  Computational Problem

So what exactly makes a problem computational?

Two main aspects to all computational problems:
• A representation  that captures  all the  relevant
  aspectsaspects ofof thethe problemproblem.
• An algorithm that solves the problem by use of the
   representation.  A  sequence   of  unambiguous
   instructions for solving a problem, i.e.,for obtaining a
  required output for any legitimate input in a finite
  amount of time. The word “algorithm”  is derived
  from  the  name   of  a  ninth  century  Arab
  mathematician, Al-Khwarizmi.


                                                                                                                                                                     7

Source slide page 8 (extracted text):
PYTHON FOR COMPUTATIONAL PROBLEM SOLVING
  MCGW Problem


Problem Statement: Man, Cabbage, Goat, Wolf Problem


A man lives on the east side of a river. He wishes to bring a cabbage,
a goat, and a wolf to a village on the west side of the river to sell.

However, his boat is only big enough to hold himself, and either the
cabbage, goat, or wolf. In addition, the man cannot leave the goat
alone with the cabbage because the goat will eat the cabbage, and
he cannot leave the wolf alone with the goat because the wolf will
eat the goat. How does the man solve his problem?
                                                                                                                                                                       8

Source slide page 9 (extracted text):
PYTHON FOR COMPUTATIONAL PROBLEM SOLVING
 MCGW Problem

Solution:

There is a simple algorithmic approach for solving this problem by simply trying all
Possible combinations of items that may be rowed back and forth across the river
to find what works.


Trying all possible solutions is referred to as a brute force approach.





                                                                                                                                                                   9

Source slide page 10 (extracted text):
PYTHON FOR COMPUTATIONAL PROBLEM SOLVING
 MCGW Problem


Computational Problem: Find a method to convert the start state (all objects
on the east of the river) to the goal state (all objects on the west side of the river)
with the constraint that certain invalid states should never be used.





                                                                                                                                                                      10

Source slide page 11 (extracted text):
PYTHON FOR COMPUTATIONAL PROBLEM SOLVING
 MCGW Problem

For example: From the start state, there are three possible moves that
can be made, only one of which results in a valid state.





                                                                                                                                                                      11

Source slide page 12 (extracted text):
PYTHON FOR COMPUTATIONAL PROBLEM SOLVING
 MCGW Problem

We check  if the new problem state is the goal state. If true, then we’ve
solved the problem in one step! (We know in our case that it isn’t, but an
algorithmic approach doesn’t have the benefit of intuition like we do)

there are only two possible moves from here:

Why Python?


• Easy to Learn: Simple readable syntax, looks similar to plain English

• Versatile: Wide range of applications - web development, data science, machine
learning, automation, game development etc.

• Extensive Libraries and Frameworks: Huge number of external libraries and modules
available for a variety of use cases

• Community Support: Large and active community of developers, extensive
documentation and tutorials available

modification

NOTES.text:
Transcript block 1 (source interval 000000-000299 seconds):
[00:00:00.600] Hello everyone, I'm Chitra GM from the Department of Computer Science and Engineering, PES University.
[00:00:07.230] The subject that I'm going to be handling is Python for Computational Problem Solving for the first year.
[00:00:13.400] As mentioned in the title itself, Computational, we are going to be dealing with the different issues revolving around computational thinking and programming.
[00:00:24.960] So what are we going to be doing in this course? What is the takeaway at the end of the course for you?
[00:00:30.230] Certainly, we are going to be teaching you programming and in a more specific language called as Python.
[00:00:37.460] More importantly, we want you to be more proficient to think computationally, to think algorithmically, at the same time to think the way computer scientists think.
[00:00:49.840] What does that mean? It means that given a problem or a challenge in hand, how will you make your computer to solve it for you?
[00:01:00.690] How will you define the different stages that are involved in order to solve a problem in such a way that you will not be doing, instead your computer is going to be doing it for you?
[00:01:11.590] That's the notion of computational thinking and algorithmic thinking.
[00:01:19.300] In order to make our computer to solve a problem for us, in your coming weeks, we are going to be dealing with the following topics.
[00:01:29.040] It starts from control structures, which includes your looping concepts, followed by data structures, which includes list, string, tuple, dictionary, sets, and so on.
[00:01:42.420] We'll also be playing around files. We will try to work with file manipulation operations.
[00:01:48.500] Following with the functions where you can make use of the built-in functions and you can also create your own set of functions and then followed by the object-oriented programming.
[00:02:00.800] So, if you want to make your computer to work for you or to solve a problem for you, what does a computer do?
[00:02:08.970] Here's my next question. Question seems a dumb question. Definitely a valid question for us.
[00:02:18.710] Computers are so amazing, it can do all sorts of work for you. You name any, it can help you out to do it. You can use computer in order to play around, play music, play games. You can ask your computer to search for certain things in case of your World Wide Web. You name anything, it will do it for you. But fundamentally, it can perform only two different things. It can do only two different things for us.
[00:02:47.620] One is called as calculation, the other one is, it can remember the results of the calculations.
[00:02:54.250] So, what type of calculations a computer can do?
[00:02:58.690] Definitely, every computer comes with a built-in operations.
[00:03:03.220] Typically, arithmetic.
[00:03:05.030] Hope you all know, arithmetic includes addition, subtraction, multiplication, and so on.
[00:03:09.450] And followed by, it can also do some simple logical operations.
[00:03:14.880] Is that enough? No.
[00:03:17.910] So, you can also create many more functions that are required for you.
[00:03:22.970] You can create your own set of operations and make your computer to solve a particular task for you.
[00:03:31.920] So, when we are talking about the task, the next immediate question would be,
[00:03:37.420] can a computer perform any task that exists in this particular world?
[00:03:42.090] Can it solve everything?
[00:03:44.280] The obvious answer is going to be no.
[00:03:47.110] The reason is limitation.
[00:03:49.460] There are limitations. To name a few, limitations could be in terms of your non-availability of the resources that are required for computing or it may be in terms of non-availability of the data required in order to perform certain tasks and so on.
[00:04:06.540] Thus, the task or a job that a computer can do can either be classified as a computational or it could be a non-computational.
[00:04:23.000] Where the problems can be solved. Non-computational means the problems that cannot be solved. In this semester, we will be dealing with the computational way of solving the problems. In order to solve a problem computationally, we need two different things. One is called as representation and the other one is called as algorithm. So let's look into representation and algorithm in depth.
[00:04:53.720] Representation is nothing but capturing all the relevant aspects of the problem.
[00:04:58.620] In order to understand it better, let's take up an example.

Transcript block 2 (source interval 000300-000599 seconds):
[00:05:04.780] The example is as follows.
[00:05:08.620] Assume that you have been allocated a task wherein you have to travel from one city to another city.
[00:05:17.280] The mode of transportation that is given to you is flight.
[00:05:22.470] In such case, if you want to travel from one city to another city,
[00:05:27.160] What is very important for you to know is what is the departure time of the flight? What is the landing time of the flight? What is the cost that is involved to travel from one city to another city? What is the distance between one city to another city and so on? At this point, I am not interested in knowing what is the color of the flight that you will be traveling? Who is the pilot?
[00:05:57.620] How many number of flight attendees are there? And so on. Thus, representation means capture all the relevant aspects, leaving out the ones that are irrelevant for us.
[00:06:10.730] Let us go and understand what is an algorithm. Let me remind you, you would have come across with the different definitions for your algorithm in your school.
[00:06:31.350] Definition that exists, but we would say it as incomplete.
[00:06:35.610] So from now onwards, we will be using the standard definition in order to describe an algorithm.
[00:06:42.340] So an algorithm is a sequence of unambiguous instructions for solving a problem, that is, for obtaining a required output for any legitimate input in a finite amount of time.
[00:06:53.940] The word algorithm is derived by a mathematician called as algorithm.
[00:07:01.110] What we will do is, we will take up an example to understand how a problem can be solved.
[00:07:14.960] The example that we are going to be looking are basically called as a river crossing problems.
[00:07:20.460] One such river crossing problems that we want to deal in today's session is called as man-cabbage-goat-wolf problem, MCGW problem.
[00:07:32.420] Let me give you a brief description of the problem and then we will try to solve it.
[00:07:40.120] Description goes as follows.
[00:07:43.000] A man lives on the east side of a river.
[00:07:47.900] He wishes to bring cabbage, goat and oolf to a village on the west side of a river to sell.
[00:07:54.660] Which means a man is standing at the one end of the river.
[00:08:00.110] And he is carrying three different items with him. The three different items are cabbage, goat, and wolf.
[00:08:07.460] His main aim is to travel from one end to the another end so that he can sell all the three different items.
[00:08:16.300] In order to go from one end to the another end, he has been given a boat.
[00:08:24.970] But there are certain constraints that exist.
[00:08:27.730] The constraint is, boat can hold man. Along with a man, it can hold only one item. An item could be cabbage, goat or wolf. In order to these, let's add few more constraints. The constraints are, man cannot leave goat and cabbage together. The reason is, goat will eat the cabbage. At the same time,
[00:08:56.980] Goat and Ulf cannot be there together because goat will be eaten by Ulf.
[00:09:03.920] So how does a man solve this problem?
[00:09:08.890] There are different solutions that exist for this particular problem.
[00:09:13.270] The simplest solution would be try with different possibilities.
[00:09:17.840] If you are solving a problem by trying with the different possibilities,
[00:09:22.020] then this approach is called as your brute force approach.
[00:09:27.250] So, what we will try to do is, we will try to take up this particular problem and solve it by hand, come back and then discuss the actual solution that is there.
[00:09:38.060] Hope you are all ready. Let's go solve this problem and then we will come back and continue our discussion in this mode.
